annotation.method: Codex read the complete local paper, surveyed its formal claims, excluded experiments and delegated results, searched the frozen mathlib and NumStability baselines, inspected every selected formula in rendered PDF pages, and built private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P03 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 40, issue 2, 2018, printed pages A817-A847

rejected_candidates.reason: Its proof is a standard dual-vector rank-one construction cited to Higham's book and is less paper-specific than equation (4.1).
Their conclusions use qualitative phrases such as sufficiently less than, approximately, and ultimately; the selected theorems provide exact finite inequalities.
The paper explicitly attributes this lemma to an earlier source rather than proving it here.

rejected_candidates.candidate: LU and GMRES specializations in sections 7-8
rejected_candidates.reason: Key solver facts are imported from earlier analyses, whereas Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 are proved in this paper under general solver contracts.

rejected_candidates.candidate: speed claims, tables, and numerical experiments
rejected_candidates.reason: They are empirical or cost claims, not finite proof targets.

T1.decision: Use equation (4.1), whose exact one-step residual identity is close to NumStability.forward_error_step_identity and requires only a small notation/orientation adapter.

T2.decision: Use Theorem 4.1's exact αᵢ/βᵢ coefficient assembly, which combines several one-step library shapes with the paper-specific four-precision solver factor.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 5.1's componentwise recurrence, which requires the paper-specific Z₁/M₁ resolvent model and a nonnegative inverse-action argument absent from the frozen library.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject experiments, speed estimates, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds and identities.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
